findings.issue: Clock skew between auth replicas. The admin replica takes the cutoff from its own clock after commit. Suppose another replica issues a token before the commit (a login that saw the old roles or ACTIVE status, or a refresh racing revokeAllSessions) and its clock runs d seconds ahead. That token's iat can then exceed the cutoff, and it keeps the pre-demote roles for up to 10 minutes. The design records this and assumes NTP, but nothing enforces or monitors it.
findings.fix: Optionally set the cutoff to now plus a small skew allowance, e.g. 2 s. The only cost is that a legitimate re-login in that window is rejected once and recovers via refresh. Otherwise state the NTP and max-skew assumption in ADR 0005 operations notes and alert on node clock offset.

findings.issue: Silent fail-open paths. If an access-deny entry is evicted (Redis maxmemory policy volatile-* or allkeys-*) or lost on a Redis restart without persistence, the revoked token is accepted and no metric fires. Any client with write access to the shared, ACL-less Redis can also delete or corrupt an entry. A non-numeric value raises NumberFormatException, which also fails open. Exposure stays bounded by the 10-minute access TTL.
findings.fix: In ADR 0005 operations, require maxmemory-policy noeviction (or a non-evicting policy for these keys) on the shared Redis. Optionally count parse failures separately from unavailability. Consider Redis ACLs that limit access-deny:* writes to auth-service when B-8 is revisited.

findings.issue: During a Redis outage both check points log a WARN on every authenticated request (the gateway at DenyListReactiveJwtDecoder.java:53 as well). An attacker or ordinary traffic can turn the outage into log amplification and extra cost. No PII is logged; the message is e.toString() only.
findings.fix: Rate-limit the WARN (e.g. once per 30 s per instance) and rely on the *.access_deny.check.unavailable counter for volume.

summary: No blocker or major issues. (1) Revocation through gateway and auth: the cutoff is taken in afterCommit, on the request thread, before the 200 is written. A login or refresh that races the admin transaction therefore gets iat <= cutoff and is rejected. iat is whole seconds, and the comparison is iat <= cutoff, so a token issued in the same second as the cutoff is conservatively revoked (an availability cost only). A null iat is revoked when an entry exists. The remaining windows are the milliseconds between DB commit and the Redis write, and cross-replica clock skew (minor finding 1). Refresh tokens are still revoked in the DB (REQUIRES_NEW), so a revoked user cannot mint a post-cutoff token except by a fresh password or Google login, which reads current status and roles from the DB. (2) Only AdminUserService.changeStatus(DISABLED) and changeRoles with a removed role write entries. Both sit behind the ADMIN-only /api/admin/** rule, and SELF_MODIFICATION and LAST_ADMIN refusals write nothing. No user-controlled path sets or extends another user's cutoff. Re-enabling never deletes the entry, and the Lua max is forward-only with tonumber coercion. (3) No Redis key injection. The key is a fixed prefix plus the signature-verified sub, the gateway decoder already applies UuidSubjectValidator before the wrapper runs, and keys travel as a binary-safe RESP argument and a Lua KEYS entry, never concatenated into a command. Null or blank sub is rejected without a lookup. (4) Fail-open is bounded. A read or write failure leaves at most today's 10-minute access TTL plus the 30 s exp skew, and the 660 s TTL covers every pre-cutoff token's lifetime. Both check points have a 500 ms Redis timeout, and the gateway follows the existing limiter's onErrorResume pattern. Eviction and corruption also fail open, without a metric (minor finding 2). (5) SecurityConfig changes only narrow access. The gateway wraps the existing decoder and auth adds one validator; no route matchers, permitAll lists or roles change. Revocation surfaces as BadJwtException or JwtValidationException, which map to 401 (proven by the G2 problem-body assertion and by the auth MockMvc test asserting AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID), not 5xx. The OIDC id-token decoding path does not use the JwtDecoder bean. (6) The common-security addition is a framework-free final class with static helpers: no bean, no auto-configuration, no new dependency. Other services' behaviour does not change. No build.gradle or dependency changes. (7) No PII. Metrics have no tags, the gateway and validator logs carry only exception text, and the write-failure log carries the user UUID, consistent with the existing admin audit log line; no email or token is logged. B-8 downstream replay is accepted residual risk per ADR 0005.
